analysis.title: Multi-Asset Strategy Daily
key_insights: Risk-off meets the oil test: USTs are supported into month-end after yesterday's rally, extending the post-FOMC move. Overnight Nasdaq futures fell about 2% after Amazon and Intel dropped sharply following earnings, adding to yesterday's weakness in Alphabet.

The key cross-asset battle for rates today is equity sell-off (bullish duration) versus oil above $116pb (inflationary). If equities extend the sell-off, 10Y UST yields may move below 4.90%, but Mizuho is reluctant to chase the rally aggressively with growth firm and oil high.
Yesterday's 3.4% Q3 US GDP print was not seen as a reason to price a materially shallower Fed hiking cycle.

ECB held rates with depo at 2.5% and delivered a dovish message (tighter financing conditions, softer growth, no material second-round wage effects), producing a front-end-led rally. Mizuho still sees December as very much alive and expects one more hike and then a pause.
Anything materially above 3% ECB terminal rate would require the energy shock to worsen without doing much damage to growth, which Mizuho calls a fairly big ask.

Euro area data today: French, Spanish, Italian and German inflation plus Q3 GDP, with Eurozone growth expected at 0.2% QoQ versus 0.6% in Q2. French data so far show hotter inflation (3.8% YoY in Oct) and negative growth (-0.1% QoQ). Softer growth with hotter inflation makes the ECB's position less comfortable and argues for caution rather than front-loading.
Gilts bull-steepened alongside USTs and EGBs, with short-end yields about 6bp lower. The Budget and revised remit support the long end through a shift toward shorter issuance.

The BoE meets next Thursday. Markets price a 25bp hike in full, with further tightening through 2027, so the question is how far the MPC thinks it needs to go. Today's DMP inflation expectations matter more than usual. Mizuho would struggle to chase Gilts aggressively while oil stays at these levels.

BoJ left its policy rate unchanged at 1.25% on an 8-1 vote. It assessed underlying inflation as broadly consistent with the 2% target and accelerated ETF sales. JGBs bull-flattened and USD/JPY fell toward 157.50.
DXY continues to fall, now around 101.80. EUR/USD is well supported near 1.1185 and GBP/USD above 1.34.
